meta.note: Compiled from public defence-news reporting, Wikipedia, and HAL statements available as of Aug 2026. Program timelines in this sector shift frequently -- treat dates as directional, not contractual, and re-verify before citing to a panel.

items.purpose: Accelerate delivery of the 180-aircraft Tejas Mk1A order via infrastructure expansion
items.status: Active; ~Rs 10,000 crore investment announced (2026) for Bengaluru/Nashik facility upgrades
items.description: HAL's largest current production priority, with expansion explicitly framed as addressing prior delivery delays.

items.project: Tejas Mk2 / Medium Weight Fighter Program
items.purpose: Develop a 4.5-gen fighter bridging Tejas Mk1A and AMCA
items.status: Prototype assembly ongoing; first flight retargeted to mid-2027
items.power_generation: Single turbofan, higher thrust class than Mk1A
items.description: Repeatedly delayed since original 2022-23 targets; now HAL's second-largest fixed-wing priority after Mk1A production.

items.status: In development under the Aeronautical Development Agency; HAL contributed early structural design work but is not the lead post-competitive-selection process
items.engine: AMCA 120 kN-class engine (Rolls-Royce proposal under negotiation)
items.description: HAL's role here is narrower than in its own programs (Tejas, LCH) -- worth noting precisely if a mentor asks, since HAL's CMD has publicly clarified the company is 'not presently involved' in the current competitive-selection phase.

items.purpose: Field India's first indigenous dedicated attack helicopter at scale
items.status: Production and delivery ongoing; 156 units on order (Army + Air Force)
items.engine: Shakti (Ardiden 1H1); HTSE-1200 as future indigenous alternative
items.description: One of HAL's two largest current order books alongside Tejas Mk1A.

items.status: Nearing operational service; final trials underway
items.description: Smaller in scale than the Prachand/Mk1A programs but operationally urgent given the age of the fleet it replaces.

items.purpose: Sustain and expand HAL's most mature helicopter platform across military and civil variants
items.status: Operational (military); civil Dhruv NG certification expected August 2026
items.mission: Utility transport, armed reconnaissance (Rudra), civil transport (Dhruv NG)
items.description: The base platform from which Rudra and, indirectly, Prachand were derived.

items.purpose: Next-generation multi-role helicopter co-developed with Safran, France, including a naval deck-based variant
items.status: Development stage; dedicated test facility established at HAL
items.description: A newer program with less public detail than Dhruv/Prachand, but notable as HAL's next major helicopter platform after the current family.

items.project: Combat Air Teaming System (CATS) / CATS Warrior
items.purpose: Establish HAL's loyal-wingman and stealth-UCAV capability across 1-tonne and 10-tonne variants
items.status: 1-tonne variant: engine-integrated, ground runs done, 2027 first flight target. 10-tonne variant: preliminary design, 2030-32 first flight target
items.mission: Manned-unmanned teaming with Tejas; strategic stealth strike (10-tonne variant)
items.description: HAL's most significant unmanned-systems program, positioning it against international loyal-wingman systems like the MQ-28 Ghost Bat.

items.purpose: Re-enter commercial aircraft manufacturing after decades of absence
items.status: Both platforms formally debuted at Wings India 2026
items.mission: Regional airline service and UDAN regional connectivity
items.description: Described in industry coverage as India's 'most serious return to civil aircraft manufacturing since the Avro era.'

items.purpose: Develop an indigenous regional transport aircraft ecosystem
items.status: Early stage; Embraer-Adani Aerospace & Defence MoU signed January 2026 to build supply chain, assembly, and indigenization roadmap
items.mission: Regional transport, competing conceptually with ATR 72, Dash 8, and similar turboprop classes
items.description: Budget breakdown includes Rs 1,000 crore earmarked specifically for systems indigenization -- a useful data point if discussing India's broader localization strategy.

items.purpose: Reduce dependency on imported engines (GE F404/F414, Safran Ardiden) across HAL's fixed-wing and rotary fleets
items.status: Active across two parallel programs (HTFE-25 turbofan, HTSE-1200 turboshaft), both moving toward endurance/certification testing through 2026
items.mission: Long-term engine supply independence for HAL's aircraft and helicopter programs
items.description: The single most directly relevant HAL initiative to GARUN's own thesis: reducing dependency on externally-sourced propulsion through indigenous, purpose-fit engine development -- a strong talking point for tying your PS1 solution to HAL's actual strategic priorities.

items.project: MALE-Class UAV Procurement & Indigenous Complementary Platforms
items.purpose: Field a large MALE UAV fleet combining import procurement with indigenous TAPAS-BH-201 and Archer-NG platforms
items.status: Active vendor competition (~24 vendors) alongside ongoing indigenous platform development
items.mission: Persistent ISR and armed MALE capability
items.platform: TAPAS-BH-201, Archer-NG, and competing imported platforms
items.description: The most directly comparable real-world program to GARUN's own PS1 target class (hybrid-electric MALE fixed-wing UAV) -- strong candidate for an opening context slide.
